review: independent bounded source review of reconstructed Rule30 inspection bridge
verdict: No blocking source defect found within reviewed scope; not accepted or qualified
scope: certificate partition boundaries, stage/workspace inclusion and complete replay routing
inspection request/process limits, structural budget accounting and absent declaration behavior
native-core refusal boundaries and preservation of large natural numbers
fixed Lean identity and adapter signature/schema validation
authoring generator registration and new-output-only adapter diagnostic
supporting_findings: Certificate text is audited before splitting; only complete renderer decodeAndAdd command boundaries are split. All command groups and original source record are retained.

All part files and final wrapper enter stage.certificates. Existing verifier loop compiles and leanchecker-replays each part, then retains exact original certificate axiom audit. Workspace helper also exposes every part in its certificate list.

Parts live outside original certificate module prefixes. Failure routing normalizes LexLeanPreserve.Parts back to original owner before B/E classification; segment boundaries avoid R1/R10 attribution collisions.

Request count/name/node/depth bounds and child output cap are enforced; adapter shares traversal fuel across names, levels and expressions across all rows, refusing unresolved fvar/mvar/level metavariables and exhausted budgets.

Absent names consume traversal budget and emit null type with empty parameters; Rust yields unrepresentable without a native candidate. Malformed or unsupported structural conversion also yields unrepresentable.
Adapter remains parsed by closed tooling schema and typechecked. Driver still executes owned signature and registry checks; inspection changes only the final entry call.
Inspection validates Lean 4.32.2 and f3b06c705e6c85f5314019d5d3baab0fec5b580c, matching embedded adapter authority.
Fifteen authored inspection functions are appended to the existing adapter authoring generator; unit assertion checks exact function values in embedded source and required registry seeds.
New adapter diagnostic writes only a new output tree and labels acceptance false; it invokes existing registry derivation rather than production export.
limitations: No Lean compilation, kernel replay, axiom audit or production qualification run performed by reviewer.
Partition unit test uses synthetic command groups; real A/B/E part elaboration/replay plus negative refusals remain required.
VR28 runtime positive/absent/budget-negative tests remain required.

Changed embedded authoring source moves compiler identity. Generated registry, adapter source equality, projections, locks and final products need coherent qualification; no current compiler pin may be adopted from this source review.
Global serde_json arbitrary_precision feature is needed for inspected large naturals but downstream regression effects were not exhaustively evaluated.
Not restoration or acceptance of the lost f01 candidate.
